themes.label: Rationale for realized-volatility forecasting framework
themes.need: Someone deciding whether to adopt a new volatility forecasting approach needs to understand why standard daily-frequency and ad hoc practitioner methods are inadequate and what benefits a realized-volatility-based framework built on high-frequency data offers.

themes.label: FX high-frequency data and volatility construction
themes.need: Someone wanting to replicate or apply the realized-volatility measure needs to know the exchange rate data source, sample period, and the procedure for constructing thirty-minute returns and aggregating them into realized volatility measures.
themes.distributed_justification: The intro paragraph (b006) previews the data source, sample dates, and empirical regularities that Section 3.1-3.2 (b031-b034) then resolves in full construction detail; same data-provenance need across the intro/§3 gap.

themes.label: Semimartingale decomposition of arbitrage-free prices
themes.need: Someone establishing the theoretical foundation for volatility measurement needs to know how an arbitrage-free asset price process decomposes into predictable mean and martingale components, and what no-arbitrage implies about jump risk.

themes.label: Quadratic variation as covariance estimator
themes.need: Someone justifying the use of realized (summed high-frequency squared/cross-product) returns as a covariance estimator needs the formal link between quadratic variation and the conditional return covariance matrix, including the conditions under which realized variation is an unbiased estimator.

themes.label: Normal-mixture distribution of returns
themes.need: Someone wanting to model the conditional distribution of returns needs to know under what conditions returns follow a normal (mixture) distribution given the realized volatility path, so density and VaR forecasts can be built on this reference distribution.

themes.label: Positive-definite trivariate realized covariance system
themes.need: Someone building a multivariate realized covariance matrix for several exchange rates needs a way to guarantee positive definiteness in higher dimensions and, for FX specifically, a way to use the no-arbitrage cross-rate identity to infer the covariance without directly modeling it.
themes.distributed_justification: Table I (b040, unrelated return-distribution content) interrupts the argument; b041 resumes and concludes the same triangular-arbitrage/cross-rate covariance-inference reasoning begun in b035-b039.

themes.label: Empirical distribution of daily FX returns
themes.need: Someone examining daily FX return behavior needs the unconditional distributional properties of raw versus realized-volatility-standardized daily returns, including moments and serial correlation, to see that standardized returns are near-Gaussian.
themes.distributed_justification: Table I (b040) precedes the Section 4 header; the §4.1 discussion of that table (b042-b045) follows contiguously; Figure 1's caption (b048) is physically interposed later (inside the Table II run-up) but is the caption for the figure discussed in b043, so it belongs to this same return-distribution need.

themes.label: Log-normality of realized volatility
themes.need: Someone deciding how to model realized volatility needs to know whether realized volatility, or its logarithm, is well approximated by a (log)normal distribution, to justify a lognormal-normal mixture return model.
themes.distributed_justification: Figure 1's caption (b048, belonging to theme t07) is physically interposed between the Table II lead-in/footnotes and the Table II results discussion; the log-volatility distribution argument resumes immediately after.

themes.label: Long-memory dynamics of realized volatility
themes.need: Someone specifying a time-series model for realized volatility needs to know the degree and nature of long-memory dependence and the cross-series correlation among the realized volatilities.

themes.label: VAR-RV model specification and estimation
themes.need: Someone wants the exact specification and in-sample estimation diagnostics of the long-memory Gaussian VAR fit to realized log-volatilities (VAR-RV), including how much the multivariate structure adds over univariate long-memory models.

themes.label: Benchmark volatility models and evaluation method
themes.need: Someone benchmarking a new volatility forecasting model needs to know which standard alternative models (VAR-ABS, AR-RV, GARCH, RiskMetrics, daily and intraday FIEGARCH) are used for comparison and the regression-based methodology used to evaluate forecast accuracy.

themes.label: VAR-RV vs benchmark forecast accuracy
themes.need: Someone deciding which volatility model to use for forecasting needs the comparative in-sample and out-of-sample accuracy results (R-squared, bias/slope tests) of VAR-RV versus GARCH-type and other benchmark forecasts at one-day and ten-day horizons.

themes.label: Why VAR-RV forecasts adapt faster
themes.need: Someone wanting to understand the source of VAR-RV's forecasting advantage needs the explanation and graphical evidence for why realized-volatility-based forecasts adapt faster to volatility shifts than GARCH or RiskMetrics forecasts.

themes.label: Measurement-error smoothing in realized volatility
themes.need: Someone concerned about measurement error in realized volatility needs to know whether and how the VAR-RV modeling approach implicitly addresses this noise without requiring an explicit smoothing or filtering step.

themes.label: Density forecast and VaR calibration
themes.need: Someone evaluating a volatility-based return density or VaR forecast needs the calibration tests (probability integral transform uniformity and independence) confirming that the lognormal-normal mixture model is well calibrated in-sample and out-of-sample.
themes.distributed_justification: Figure 7's caption (b103) is separated from its in-text reference (b101, independence/PIT discussion) by the Conclusions section heading; both serve the single density-forecast-calibration need.

themes.label: Future research directions for realized volatility
themes.need: Someone looking to extend this realized-volatility framework needs the paper's concrete proposed research directions: explicit jump modeling, alternative predictive distributions, other risk measures, extension to other asset classes, positive-definite high-dimensional (Cholesky) parameterization, and factor structure.

unassigned.reason: Mini-abstract recapping the paper's overall empirical findings (VAR-RV model, forecast superiority, density calibration) spanning topics fully resolved by dedicated downstream themes (t10, t12, t13, t15); no single realistic search need matches this multi-topic recap paragraph on its own.
